rows.title: CT reports progress on underfunded state employee pension funds
rows.standfirst: Connecticut’s once-neglected state-employee pension system is now 55% funded — up from 38% eight years ago, but still a national laggard.

rows.title: Report: About half of the population lacks economic security
rows.standfirst: A family of four in the northeast needed to earn close to $151,100 in 2022 to be economically secure, according to an Urban Institute report.

rows.title: Report: ‘Guardrails’ send big money to pensions; program funds lag
rows.standfirst: Even though its finances have stabilized, Connecticut’s “fiscal guardrails” have evolved beyond their stated purpose, a new report claims.

rows.title: Report: Half of CT’s set-aside ‘volatile’ funds are actually stable
rows.standfirst: A report from Connecticut Voices for Children says the state could dedicate $755M more yearly for education, human services and town aid.

rows.title: BEST OF 2024: A question of volatility: Are Connecticut’s fiscal guardrails in the right place?
rows.standfirst: The first in a three-part series about Connecticut’s fiscal guardrails and their impact not only on state reserves and debt, but also core programs like education and health care.
